title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Earlier pages build a local theory of how a graph K drawn on a conformal surface is seen from each of its sides ('rives'). The Scholie on the previous page notes that each side gives K its own real-analytic structure, and that these structures need not agree with one another or with how K sits in C. Th. 3, referred to here, appears to be the 'cutting' theorem: cutting a conformal surface along K produces a conformal surface with boundary. Lemma 2 introduced the gluing function between the two sides of an edge.

Th. 4 (stated as a programme: 'on doit avoir un théorème dans ce style là'). It proposes an equivalence of categories between two categories.

(a) Triples (X, K, S):
- X is a compact conformal (Riemann) surface with boundary.
- (K, S) is a compact topological 1-complex (a graph) with vertex set S, and ∂X ⊂ K ⊂ X.
- K is 'sufficiently regular', e.g. piecewise rectifiable.
- The NB in the margin allows edges that are circles without vertices, not only arcs.

(b) Gluing data (X̃, S̃, σ):
- X̃ is a conformal surface with compact boundary.
- S̃ is a finite subset of ∂X̃.
- σ is an involution of Déc(∂X̃/S̃), the boundary 'cut open' at the points of S̃ (a disjoint union of closed arcs and circles).
- σ is sufficiently regular.
- Arcs fixed pointwise by σ should correspond to ∂X. An arc folded onto itself would give a dangling edge of K ending in the interior of X. Pairs of arcs exchanged by σ give interior edges of K.

Functor (a)→(b). Normalize, i.e. cut X along K (Th. 3). One then needs a complement saying how regular the gluing function of Lemma 2 is.

Functor (b)→(a). Form the topological quotient X = X̃/R, where R is the equivalence relation generated by σ. Give X the structure sheaf of continuous functions that are holomorphic on X∖K ≅ X̃∖∂X̃.

The next page reduces the claim that this sheaf is a conformal structure with boundary, and that it gives back X̃, to two model cases (Lemma 3). In those cases a half-disc is glued to a half-disc along a rectifiable homeomorphism [0,1]→[0,1] (or [−1,1]→[−1,1]) that is regular near 0.

In modern terms this is conformal welding packaged functorially. A conformal surface together with a cut graph is equivalent to the cut-open surface together with boundary-identification data. The problem it serves is 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes': cutting and pasting Riemann surfaces along graphs. This is the analytic counterpart of the dessins / ribbon-graph cut-and-paste of the Esquisse period.
errors: The regularity hypotheses are left vague ('assez régulier', 'rectifiable par morceaux'), and they do not obviously match on the two sides. Rectifiability of K in X is not a natural intrinsic condition on the welding homeomorphism σ. The classical good class for weldings is quasisymmetric homeomorphisms (giving quasiarcs), and rectifiable curves need not have quasisymmetric weldings. As stated, then, the two categories are not obviously equivalent; the theorem needs a careful matching of regularity classes.

In the inverse functor, defining the structure sheaf as continuous functions holomorphic off K yields a conformal structure only if gluing along σ is solvable. Uniqueness, and recovering the structure of X, also requires K to be removable for continuous holomorphic functions. Rectifiable (σ-finite length) curves are removable by Painlevé/Besicovitch, so uniqueness is fine in the rectifiable case. Existence for an arbitrary 'rectifiable' homeomorphism σ is not automatic, which is exactly the content deferred to Lemma 3.
Morphisms of the two categories are not specified; presumably isomorphisms only, or conformal maps respecting K.
Folded arcs (σ reversing an arc onto itself) and circle-edges need separate local models. The NB acknowledges circles, but the folded case is not discussed.

ideas.what: Equivalence between (surface, embedded graph containing the boundary) and (cut-open surface, finite boundary set, involution of the cut boundary): cut-and-paste of conformal surfaces as an equivalence of categories
ideas.modern_name: conformal welding / sewing of Riemann surfaces; normalization along a graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960) for conformal welding; sewing formulations by Segal, Huang, Radnell–Schippers
ideas.where_published: Spirit of cut-and-paste in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this precise statement not known to be published

ideas.what: Structure sheaf on the glued space defined as continuous functions holomorphic off the gluing graph
ideas.modern_name: conformal removability of the welding curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Painlevé, Besicovitch (removability of rectifiable sets for continuous holomorphic functions); Jones, Bishop on removability and non-uniqueness of weldings

ideas.what: Allowing edges that are circles without vertices, and a boundary 'cut at S' Déc(∂X̃/S̃) carrying an involution
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial gluing data, close to ribbon-graph / pants-type gluing data

missed.claim: A functorial equivalence between Riemann surfaces with embedded low-regularity graphs and boundary-gluing data (involutions on the cut boundary). This anticipates the sewing formalism of conformal field theory with non-smooth boundary parametrizations (Segal; Radnell–Schippers quasisymmetric sewing) and links it to Grothendieck's dessins-type cut-and-paste. The page also isolates the right problem: matching regularity classes of K and σ.
missed.quote: Th. 4 Équivalence de catégories entre a) Cat. des couples (X, K, S) ... b) Cat des systèmes (X̃, S̃, σ) ... σ une involution de Déc(∂X̃/S̃)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical: the mathematics is now standard conformal welding theory. It documents Grothendieck working, around 1983–84, on analytic surgery of Riemann surfaces parallel to the Esquisse programme.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a categorical packaging of conformal welding and cut-and-paste along graphs. The analytic core (welding, removability) predates it and is well known, and the regularity issues are left open. It is interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's analytic 'chirurgie' programme, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: '(lorsque)' after 'faisceau structural conforme' is doubtful; it may be '(évident)' or similar, and the phrase likely reads 'on munit d'un faisceau structural conforme'.
The marginal NB reads approximately: 'NB On ne suppose pas nécessairement les arêtes de K, S des intervalles (il peut y avoir des cercles)'.
The regularity condition reads approximately '(rectifiable p. morceaux?)'; the word after 'rectifiable' is uncertain in the image.
'compacte' in (a) and the inserted 'compact' in (b) refer to the compactness of the surface and of its boundary respectively; the inserted 'compact' above 'complexe top.' replaces a struck-out word.
